f.title: Consider the listed factors when reviewing the need for additional actions
f.statement: When reviewing the need for additional actions in the Pharmacovigilance Plan and Risk Minimization Plan, the MAH should consider: impact, severity, frequency, reversibility and preventability of severe ADRs; severity of the indicated disease and severity and background incidence of complications; estimated patient exposure; identified risk populations; expected benefits of risk minimisation; treatment duration; worldwide authorisation status; results of overseas surveillance and studies; differences in safety profile between Japan and overseas; and safety measures taken overseas.
f.applicability: Draft (not in force; preceded the final RMP Guidance notified on 11 Apr 2012). MHLW draft Risk Management Plan (RMP) Guidance of 2 Aug 2011 for new drugs at approval review and during the re-examination period, newly submitted Safety Specifications for generics and drugs after re-examination, and generics whose reference drug has additional risk minimisation activities; English translation by PMDA provided for reference only (the Japanese original prevails)

rows.quote:
7. In the "Pharmacovigilance Plan" and "Risk Minimization Plan", when the MAH reviews
the need of additional actions, the following should be considered.

7-1. The impact of ADRs, the severity, frequency, reversibility and preventability on
severe ADRs
  7-2. The severity of disease included in drug indications, the severity and the
background incidence rate of complications

7-3. Estimated number of patient exposure

7-4. Identified risk populations

7-5. Expected benefits by conducting risk minimization activity

7-6. Treatment duration

7-7. World-wide market authorization status

7-8. Results of overseas surveillance and studies (if it is changed, the points which
should be taken into account)

7-9. The difference in safety profiles between Japan and overseas

7-10. Safety measures which was taken in overseas
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: below 90: long enumerated list; translation; Japanese original may be binding (こと); superseded/draft version; no previous_key link to the current baseline.

f.statement: When setting milestones the MAH should consider when AEs of a pre-defined frequency will be detected at a predetermined reliability level (defining a frequency reflecting the level acceptable to patients and public health), when risk factors can be evaluated accurately, when results of ongoing or proposed safety studies will be available, and when the severity and significance of risks in the Risk Minimization Plan will be assessed — early and frequently if the risk is extremely severe.
f.clause: IV.4 List of the Pharmacovigilance plan
f.applicability: Draft (not in force; preceded the final RMP Guidance notified on 11 Apr 2012). rows.quote:
When the MAH sets up milestones, the following should be considered:


- When will AEs with pre-defined frequency at the predetermined reliability level be
detected? The MAH should define the frequency reflecting the acceptable level of the
patients and public health.


- When will the MAH be able to evaluate accurately the risk factors which affect to onset
of AEs?


- When will the result of ongoing or proposed safety study be available?


- When will the assessment of the severity and significance of the risk that is included in
Risk Minimization Plan be performed? If the risk is extremely severe, it is necessary
to assess the effect of risk minimization activity early in a frequent manner.
